title: Instrumentation for split-testing batching/cache policies with econ heatmaps and SLO-triggered rollback
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Build end-to-end instrumentation and dashboards to run safe split-tests of batching and cache (prefix/KV) config recommendations, and to enable automated, SLO-driven rollback when experiments degrade latency/correctness or increase cost without commensurate quality uplift. This ticket covers metric definitions, experiment tagging, per-cohort econ heatmap generation, a statistical analysis pipeline, and a dashboard + alert set that gates automated rollback. This is scoped to hosted API traffic and Dedicated canary pools for the initial rollout.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Events and telemetry added to request pipeline to capture batch size, cache hit/miss, prefetch decisions, config variant id, model variant id, and per-request token counts.
2) Daily-aggregated per-cohort econ heatmap available in Grafana/Looker showing cost, throughput, latency, and quality delta.
3) Statistical pipeline produces uplift estimates with 95% credible intervals and flags statistically significant regressions/benefits.
4) SLO-triggered guard implemented: automated rollback when p95 latency increases >15% OR error rate increases >0.5% absolute OR semantic-quality regression exceeds defined threshold.
5) Run one internal experiment with a saved report and postmortem attached.
6) Dashboard docs and runbook added to Confluence with step-by-step rollback and evaluation steps.
metrics: unit_cost_per_1k_tokens: per-variant cost normalized by tokens and GPU-time
p95_latency_ms: tail latency at 95th percentile computed per 5-minute window
request_error_rate_pct: fraction of requests with non-2xx or model runtime errors
cache_hit_rate_pct: prefix/KV cache hit fraction (per-request and per-token basis)
avg_batch_size: mean microbatch size observed by the runtime
quality_regression_score: fraction of eval prompts with degraded output (embedding cosine drop > 0.04 or heuristic mismatch), computed per-cohort
throughput_rps: requests per second per shard for capacity accounting
experiment_design: We will use randomized assignment at the routing layer with deterministic sticky hashing for user/request-id cohorts. Variants: baseline (current batch/cache heuristics), variant-A (aggressive prefetch + higher microbatch default), variant-B (conservative prefetch + smaller microbatch). Run for minimum 72h to cover diurnal traffic and require minimum N requests per cohort (adaptive N based on cohort traffic — see statistical pipeline). Analysis will use a hierarchical Bayesian uplift estimator to borrow strength across slices and compute credible intervals for cost and quality metrics. For fast safety gates (minutes), use streaming monitors for p95 latency and error rate with precomputed thresholds. For final evaluation use daily aggregated posterior summaries. Cohorts: new customers, high-QPS sessions, embedding-heavy flows, short-sequence chat, long-sequence generation. Seed cohort definitions in the runbook.
dashboard_components: Econ heatmap: x-axis = cohort, y-axis = variant, color = unit_cost_per_1k_tokens, overlays for quality_regression_score and p95 latency
Time-series: per-variant p50/p90/p95 latency, throughput, error rate
Cohort table: traffic share, cache_hit_rate, avg_batch_size, cost delta vs baseline
Statistical results panel: uplift posterior median, 95% CI, probability(benefit>0) and probability(harm>threshold)
Safety gates panel: live boolean indicators for SLO breaches and recent rollbacks
Drilldown link: sample failing requests and PR link to applied config
tasks: Add variant_id and policy metadata tags at router and runtime (ENG runtime instrumentation)
Emit cache ops (hit/miss/prefetch) and batch composition events to Kafka topic 'telemetry.experiments'
Build aggregation job in Dataflow to produce per-variant/cohort daily tables
Implement hierarchical Bayesian pipeline using ArviZ/Stan or pyro primer notebook and expose results via scheduled job
Create Grafana dashboard panels and Looker derived tables for heatmap
Implement streaming SLO monitors using existing alerting infra and wire to rollback controller
Add runbook and experiment template in Confluence with checklist and QA steps
Execute internal canary experiment and produce final report
risks: Data sparsity in low-traffic cohorts could yield noisy uplift estimates — mitigation: pool with hierarchical model and require min-traffic guard
Telemetry tagging bugs may misattribute requests — mitigation: staging validation with traffic replay (ENG-28199)
Aggressive configs could silently degrade semantic quality — mitigation: cohorted eval prompts and embedding-based drift detection
Autoscaling interactions with Dedicated pools may change cost math — mitigation: run isolated canaries and consult capacity team
False positives from monitors could trigger unnecessary rollback — mitigation: debounce windows and require multi-metric confirmation
